Subject: Re: Governing law selection & injunctive relief carve-in — Brightly MSA/Order Form

Vanessa,

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal asked us to confirm the governing law and injunctive relief language before procurement signs. Brightly has an internal policy preferring our state (Massachusetts) for choice-of-law and wants to keep a clear path to injunctive relief in local courts without having to go to arbitration first. That said, we don’t want to block e-signing indefinitely — can your legal team propose a compromise?

High-level asks from our side:
- Governing law: Massachusetts (our HQ)
- Injunctive relief: emergency remedies may be sought in MA state/federal court before arbitration if needed
- No broad waiver of remediation rights; limited carveout for injunctive relief only

Can we get Redwood’s preferred wording and any operational impacts (support, regional enforcement) so procurement can move forward?

Thanks,
Samantha Irving
Sr. Procurement Manager
Brightly Health

Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Diego (sales ops) to propose practical language. Two quick things from our side:

Subject: RE: Governing law selection & injunctive relief carve-in — Brightly MSA/Order Form

Samantha / team —

Thanks for the note. I attached a redline (Redwood_MSA_track_changes_20261118.docx) with a proposed middle-ground. Summary below: 

Proposed compromise (high-level):
- Choice of law: California (Redwood’s default), with an express recognition that seeking interim injunctive relief in the customer’s local court (MA) is permitted for the limited purpose of preserving the status quo or protecting confidential information.
- Forum for injunctive relief: customer may seek emergency equitable relief in MA courts; such relief shall not be considered a waiver of Redwood’s right to arbitration for other disputes.
- Notice & cure: customer must provide expedited notice to Redwood and allow 48 hours for Redwood to respond unless immediate relief is demonstrably required.
- Limited scope: carveout strictly limited to injunctive relief (e.g., temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction) and does not expand damages/monetary relief in MA courts.
- Enforcement cooperation: Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to assist (e.g., provide logs, engineers) under existing data-request process and protective order if requested by court.

Rationale: preserves Redwood’s arbitration posture and centralized governing law while giving Brightly a practical path to emergency remedies locally. This tends to be acceptable to enterprise buyers who want operational certainty in their home jurisdiction.

Alex — please confirm if Brightly’s counsel is comfortable with the notice period and scope limitation.

I’ve left track changes in the attached. If procurement is happy, we can finalize the Order Form signature blocks and route to DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_track_changes_20261118.docx (redline of Sections 12-15)

Subject: Re: Governing law selection & injunctive relief carve-in — Brightly MSA/Order Form

Marissa / Vanessa —

Thanks for the redline. Brightly’s counsel reviewed and has two comments:
1) We prefer bracketed language allowing choice-of-law to be Massachusetts if both parties agree, or California if not — essentially a mutual election, but Brightly wants the default to be MA where the parties have an ongoing relationship.
2) The 48-hour notice is tight for some emergency scenarios. Can Redwood accept wording that permits expedited relief without rigid cure timing "where delay would cause irreparable harm," while still encouraging notice?

If you can accept a small tweak on the 48-hour notice language and consider mutual-default language for choice-of-law, we can get procurement to sign quickly.

Alex Reed
Partner, Brightly Law Group

Subject: Re: Governing law selection & injunctive relief carve-in — Brightly MSA/Order Form

All —

Thanks for the quick review. Team notes:
- Redwood will accept a mutual-election approach: if Brightly prefers MA and both sides sign/initial that box on the Order Form, governing law will be MA; absent that, default to California. We’ll add the bracketed election on the Order Form and call it out in the signature worksheet.
- On the notice/cure: Marissa will change the 48-hour line to require "expedited notice and reasonable opportunity to respond where practicable," and retain an express exception that in cases of demonstrable irreparable harm, the customer may seek immediate interim relief.
- Final ask from Brightly: confirmation that Redwood will not object to expedited evidentiary preservation requests for the narrow injunctive relief carveout. Marissa confirms Redwood will follow its standard evidence-preservation process and execute protective orders as needed.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to edit the attached redline with the two tweaks (bracketed election + softened notice language).
2) Vanessa/Aditya to approve final commercial terms.
3) Diego to prepare Order Form with election checkbox and DocuSign link.

If that works I’ll ask procurement to circulate an internal sign-off and we’ll route for signature tomorrow.

V

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
